inputs.share_count_basis: 51.587M basic on the 10-Q cover page dated 2026-07-31 (51.585M at the 2026-06-30 balance sheet) plus ~0.6M treasury-method dilution from RSUs/options (Q2 2026 weighted diluted 52.267M vs basic ~52.2M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $1B/24-month buyback (FY2025 $662M, H1-2026 $409M incl. the $300M Morgan Stanley ASR) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, and that cash is already charged as SBC. Any further ASR share delivery at final settlement lowers the count and would raise per-share value slightly.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement stock-based compensation add-back $176.8M plus $26.8M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities); EPAM publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure in its non-GAAP reconciliation, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026: $96.3M + $22.9M = $119.2M (4.2% of revenue).
inputs.interest_income_source: Estimated. EPAM tags only a net 'Interest and other income, net' line (us-gaap NonoperatingGainsLosses: $46.9M FY2024, $11.5M FY2025, -$0.2M H1-2026) which nets FX and other items against interest. The interest component is estimated at ~3.2% on ~$1.2B average FY2025 cash. Stripped because net cash ($764M) is ~2x the owner-FCF base; the cash pile is added back once in the equity bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $662.2M (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); H1-2026 $409.0M. Actual cash, not the $1B authorisation.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (latest close; US market not yet open on the valuation date)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD rate: 10-year Treasury ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.3 (EPAM has traded at 1.3-1.5x market volatility since the 2022 Ukraine shock and the 2026 AI-disruption de-rating) gives a cost of equity ~10.7%; debt is $25M against $789M cash so WACC ~10.5%. No separate AI-risk premium is stacked on top: the structural risk that AI shrinks billable hours is charged once, through the bear driver path and a 30% bear weight, not twice through the discount rate as well. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside EBITDA as an operating expense (operating lease liabilities $119M at FY2025), so the lease charge is already in the flows; lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial at EPAM (single-digit $M); no NCI deduction and no attributable-flow adjustment.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), scenario-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods: EPAM is an operating IT-services/digital-engineering company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the non-FCF rows apply, and the US-tech adaptations file is not needed (USD filer, USD quote, leases inside EBITDA, no NCI, SBC-paying market). First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 is FY2025 (last completed year); year 1 is FY2026 at the midpoint of the lowered guidance (3.2-4.2% reported). EBITDA margin path is pre-SBC, pre-D&A: GAAP EBITDA + SBC was 15.1% in FY2025 and 15.2% in H1-2026; management guides adjusted operating margin (pre-SBC, pre-amortisation, pre-one-offs) to the high end of 15-16%, which is ~1pp of recurring 'one-off' cost (severance, acquisition costs, war-related) above the GAAP-based figure that this build charges as real. D&A 2.3% of revenue is mostly acquired-intangible amortisation ($71.4M FY2025 from the NEORIS/First Derivative deals) rolling off; capex is only 0.8% ($42M). Cash taxes of $184M on $506M pretax (36%) in FY2025 and $196M on $584M (34%) in FY2024 run well above the ~24% book rate (Section 174 R&D capitalisation, foreign withholding on repatriation); the cash rate ramps 31% -> 25% as Section 174 expensing is restored. Working capital is charged on the change in revenue at -10% because a time-and-materials business carries ~19% of revenue in receivables against ~9% in accrued comp/payables. Buybacks fund the flat count (repurchaser). Belarus cash (~$37M) is subject to the April 2024 dividend-repatriation restrictions and is deducted in the equity bridge; Ukraine cash (~$39M) is not restricted and is left in net cash.

equity_bridge.item: Belarus-held cash subject to dividend restrictions
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K: ~$37M of cash held in Belarusian banks cannot be freely distributed to US shareholders under the April 2024 Belarusian restrictions; haircut to zero pending relief. ~$39M in Ukrainian banks is not restricted and stays in net cash.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, cross-checked against FY2026 guidance (3.2-4.2% reported, 2-3% organic constant currency). Equity 5yr CAGR (13.2%) is inflated by the 2020-22 digital boom and the 3yr figure (7.0%) is depressed by $1.2B of buybacks since 2023, so neither is a clean forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.2% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 2.9% and from revenue 3yr CAGR 4.2%: the 2020-2022 boom (revenue +41% in FY2021, +28% in FY2022) is still inside the 5-year window while the 2023-2025 period was flat-to-recovering. The 3-year revenue CAGR is the anchor.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr). Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC incl. equity-award taxes - interest income: FY2020 $376M (475.6 - 95.4 - ~4), FY2022 $244M (382.5 - 126.5 - ~12), FY2025 $371M (612.7 - 203.6 - ~38). Interest income before FY2024 is estimated from average cash and prevailing short rates (not separately tagged); the CAGRs move <1pp on any plausible alternative. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (-0.3%) sits far below reported FCF (+5.2%): SBC incl. withholding grew from $95M (2.8% of revenue) in FY2020 to $204M (3.7%) in FY2025, so an increasing share of reported cash generation is being paid to employees in stock. FY2025 owner FCF also benefited from strong Q3-Q4 collections after H1 working-capital build; H1-2026 reported FCF was -$72M on the usual bonus-payment seasonality.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the 3.7% guidance midpoint; FY2027-29 at 4-5% as the AI-led large deals management pushed to H1 2027 convert partially and Financial Services keeps growing low-double-digits while Software & Hi-Tech keeps shrinking; then a glide to 2.5% as AI productivity compresses billable hours roughly in line with volume growth. Well below the 15.5% five-year revenue CAGR, which was a boom.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 15.5% in FY2026 (guidance: adjusted operating margin at the high end of 15-16%, less ~1pp recurring 'one-off' cost, plus ~1pp depreciation) drifting to 16.5% on delivery-mix shift to India/LatAm and AI-assisted utilisation gains that EPAM partly keeps. SBC anchored at 3.9% (FY2025 3.7%, H1-2026 4.2% incl. withholding) and eased 0.1pp/yr to 3.0%. Cash tax ramps from 31% to 25% as Section 174 expensing returns.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.5% terminal growth and a 15x owner-FCF cap: a labour-based services business facing AI deflation does not earn a 20x mature-compounder multiple.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of FY2026 guidance, then the AI-native pipeline (AI/RUN, DIALX, Anthropic partnership; >$105M AI-native revenue in a single quarter already) converts on schedule in H1 2027 and North America recovers, taking growth to high-single/low-double digits in FY2028-29 before maturing. Still below the FY2016-2021 20%+ era.
bull.margin_rationale: Outcome-based AI engagements let EPAM keep a share of the productivity gain: pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 18%, roughly the FY2019-21 level, on lower-cost delivery mix and pricing rather than headcount.

bear.growth_rationale: Bottom of FY2026 guidance, then the Software & Hi-Tech pattern (clients using AI tooling in-house, cutting external engineering hours) spreads to Financial Services and Consumer from FY2027: billable hours per project fall faster than EPAM can sell new scope, revenue declines ~4%/yr for two years and only stabilises at 1.5-2% nominal growth by FY2033. A Belarus/Ukraine escalation is not separately modelled but would sit inside this path.
bear.margin_rationale: Pricing deflation and bench cost during the contraction compress pre-SBC EBITDA to 12% (the FY2023-24 trough was ~14%); SBC stays sticky at ~3.9% because retention pay does not fall with revenue. Terminal cap cut to 12x and growth to 1.5% for a shrinking labour-arbitrage franchise.

scenario_narratives.base: EPAM's axes are (1) whether generative-AI coding tools shrink billable hours faster than AI-native transformation work replaces them, (2) whether the large AI-led enterprise deals management now dates to H1 2027 actually convert, (3) Financial Services growth versus Software & Hi-Tech decline, and (4) the Ukraine/Belarus delivery tail. Base: FY2026 lands at the 3.7% guidance midpoint with adjusted margins at the high end of 15-16%; from FY2027 the AI-native pipeline converts partially and Financial Services carries the book while Hi-Tech keeps shrinking, giving 4-5% growth that fades to 2.5% by FY2035 as AI productivity is largely passed to clients. Pre-SBC EBITDA edges from 15.5% to 16.5% on delivery-mix shift; SBC eases from 3.9% to 3.0% of revenue; cash tax normalises from 31% to 25%. The $1B buyback funds a flat 52.2M share count. Net cash of $764M (less $37M restricted in Belarus) is added once.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to be a demand multiplier for EPAM rather than a deflator: the Anthropic partnership and AI/RUN platform make EPAM the engineering partner of choice for enterprise AI rollouts, the pushed-out large deals convert in H1 2027, North American discretionary spend recovers, and outcome-based pricing lets EPAM keep part of the productivity gain. Growth runs 7-9% in FY2027-29 before maturing to 3%; pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 18% (the FY2019-21 level). Terminal growth 3%, same 15x cap and 10.5% WACC as base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Software & Hi-Tech vertical is the leading indicator: AI-savvy clients are already cutting external engineering hours and building in-house, and from FY2027 Financial Services and Consumer clients follow as AI tooling matures. Time-and-materials revenue falls ~4%/yr for two years while EPAM carries bench cost and pricing deflation; pre-SBC EBITDA compresses to 12% and SBC stays sticky at ~3.9% of revenue. The business stabilises as a smaller, slower franchise (1.5% terminal growth, 12x cap). This path is also where a Ukraine/Belarus escalation, further large-deal slippage, or trapped-cash losses would land.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (outcome-based AI-native pricing replacing billable hours), the bear pattern is already visible in the Software & Hi-Tech vertical, management has already slipped the AI-deal conversion timeline once (late 2026 -> H1 2027), and EPAM carries a geopolitical delivery tail (14,100 staff in Ukraine/Belarus) no large peer shares. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right: deal conversion on the revised schedule, a North American demand recovery, and a pricing model that captures AI productivity for EPAM rather than the client. Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC (incl. withholding taxes) fully expensed, interest income on the cash pile stripped, share count held flat, and a 10-year component build so the margin and tax paths have matured before Gordon growth is applied. The company is valued as a labour-based services franchise in structural transition, not as a software compounder: the terminal cap is 15x (12x bear), terminal growth 2.5%, and the AI-disruption risk is expressed through a 30% bear weight rather than a discount-rate premium so it is charged once. The 2026 de-rating (52-week range 73-223) is the market pricing something between the bear and base paths; the finding is whether the weighted value clears the price by enough to compensate for the bear-case downside.
key_risks_to_valuation: Generative-AI productivity reducing billable hours per project faster than AI-native revenue replaces them (structural, the bear axis)
Further slippage of the large AI-led deals now dated to H1 2027; management has already moved this once
Software & Hi-Tech vertical decline spreading to Financial Services and Consumer as those clients build in-house
Ukraine/Belarus escalation disrupting ~14,100 delivery staff, the owned Kyiv building, and ~$76M of in-country cash
Cash tax rate staying near 35% rather than normalising to 25% (Section 174 timing, foreign withholding)
Interest income is estimated, not tagged; a higher true figure would lower the owner-FCF base modestly
Buyback executed at prices above intrinsic value would destroy value the flat-count convention does not capture; the H1-2026 debt draw ($165M at Q1) to fund the ASR was repaid by Q2
Working-capital seasonality: H1 FCF is routinely negative on bonus payments; the annual figure is the right base
